Chapter 10: The Beauty of Asymmetry and the Wisdom of Accepting Imbalance
Have you ever noticed how life is almost never fair—or perfectly balanced? Some folks are born with all sorts of advantages, while others face tough challenges right from the start. Opportunities don’t always come evenly, and let’s be honest—luck plays a much bigger part than we’d like to admit. We all crave a sense of symmetry, a world where things are equal and predictable. But that’s just not the reality we live in.
Picture someone who always works hard and follows all the so-called rules, expecting that effort will naturally lead to rewards. When things don’t turn out as planned, it’s easy to feel frustrated—almost like the universe has broken a promise. But, as time goes on, we realize life is packed with imbalances. Some are good, some are tough to swallow, but all of them are simply part of the deal.
Most of us don’t even realize how much we push back against this idea of asymmetry. We want life to make sense—to follow some kind of neat pattern. But think about it—the biggest things in our lives, like love, loss, success, and failure, hardly ever show up in equal amounts. They don’t follow a schedule, and they certainly aren’t fair.
So, what’s the healthiest way to deal with all this? It’s learning to accept imbalance and choosing to work with it, instead of fighting against it.
Imagine a musician trying to master their craft. Progress doesn’t come in a straight line. Some days, inspiration just flows. Other days, it’s nothing but frustration and self-doubt. The path is full of ups and downs, but that’s exactly what makes it meaningful. The real beauty lies in the unpredictability—in those bursts of grace that you simply can’t plan for.
Over time, it becomes clear: wisdom isn’t about forcing the world to be what we want. It’s about accepting things as they are. It means letting go of that constant need for perfect balance, and instead, finding meaning in the unevenness of life.
There’s a quiet kind of freedom in embracing asymmetry. It opens you up to surprises, to luck, and to those unexpected gifts and challenges that shape your story. In the end, the most beautiful moments tend to arrive out of nowhere—unplanned, unpredictable, and all the more precious because of it.
